body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(a\in J\), define
\[
 h_n(a)=\left\{\frac{4\kappa(a)}{n f(a)\theta'(a)^2}\right\}^{1/3}.
\]
Then \(h_n(a)>0\) and, uniformly in \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(a\in J\),
\[
 \left(\frac{4v_\kappa}{C_gC_\theta^2}\right)^{1/3}
 \le n^{1/3}h_n(a)
 \le
 \left(\frac{4V_\kappa}{c_gc_\theta^2}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
The coordinate
\[
 \Psi_{n,P}(a)=\int_{\inf J}^{a}h_n(v)^{-1}\,dv
\]
is bi-Lipschitz and maps \(J\) onto an interval of exact length
\[
 \Psi_{n,P}(\sup J)=n^{1/3}\int_J
 \left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}da
 =T_n(P).
\]
This is an exact spatial-clock identity; it does not assert a coupling of \(S_n\) or \(S_n^\circ\) to a canonical growing-domain maximum.
body.justification: Derives the exact local cube-root scale and spatial-volume clock under explicit positivity conditions.
body.gap: No growing-domain coupling or cross-fitted optimized-value stability is proved.
body.consumer: The clock is an algebraic coordinate, not an observed-statistic limit theorem.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(a\in J\).  By \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\), \(\int p(w)\,dw=1\), and by \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\),
\(
 c_g\le g(a\mid w)\le C_g
\)
for every \(w\).  Since \(p\ge0\), the definition of \(f\) gives
\[
 c_g=c_g\int p(w)\,dw
 \le f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw
 \le C_g\int p(w)\,dw=C_g. \tag{1}
\]
The assumptions \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\) and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\) give
\[
 0<c_\theta\le\theta'(a)\le C_\theta,
 \qquad
 0<v_\kappa\le\kappa(a)\le V_\kappa. \tag{2}
\]
Thus every factor divided by in the definition of \(h_n(a)\) is strictly positive.  Combining (1)--(2), with division only by positive quantities, yields
\[
 \left(\frac{4v_\kappa}{nC_gC_\theta^2}\right)^{1/3}
 \le h_n(a)\le
 \left(\frac{4V_\kappa}{nc_gc_\theta^2}\right)^{1/3}. \tag{3}
\]
Multiplication by \(n^{1/3}>0\) proves the first displayed bound in the theorem.

Inverting the positive defining expression gives
\[
 h_n(a)^{-1}=n^{1/3}
 \left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}. \tag{4}
\]
Taking reciprocals in (3) places the right side of (4) between
\[
 n^{1/3}\left(\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right)^{1/3}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 n^{1/3}\left(\frac{C_gC_\theta^2}{4v_\kappa}\right)^{1/3}. \tag{5}
\]
For \(a_1<a_2\) in \(J\), integrating (5) gives
\[
 n^{1/3}\left(\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right)^{1/3}(a_2-a_1)
 \le \Psi_{n,P}(a_2)-\Psi_{n,P}(a_1)
 \le n^{1/3}\left(\frac{C_gC_\theta^2}{4v_\kappa}\right)^{1/3}(a_2-a_1). \tag{6}
\]
Both constants are finite and strictly positive, so \(\Psi_{n,P}\) is strictly increasing and bi-Lipschitz.  Since \(\Psi_{n,P}(\inf J)=0\), its image is an interval whose length is \(\Psi_{n,P}(\sup J)\).  Integrating (4) and using \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) proves the exact identity
\[
 \Psi_{n,P}(\sup J)
 =n^{1/3}\int_J
 \left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}\,da
 =n^{1/3}\mathcal V(P)=T_n(P). \tag{7}
\]
All constants in (3), (5), and (6) depend only on the fixed model constants.  The bounds are therefore uniform over \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(a\in J\).  The proof is entirely observed-law algebra and makes no coupling or stochastic-transfer assertion.
